translations.en: @7rAnselm@0r takes your hand, says those words,
then leaves to help @7rBeatrix@0r.
In the end, it seems fighting is the only way to protect the seal.
Perhaps it is enough that you now have the resolve to do so.
Are you ready? Then let's go.
There's no time to dawdle. Let's hurry.
About that @3rPsalm@0r...
This time, the request comes from me. Is that all right?
Having deciphered it, I've concluded that some sort of item
has been hidden away.
Probably as a precaution against an emergency.
And judging by what we've seen so far,
I think the names in the psalm are place names.
The three names are Cocosnoot, Amandel, and Walnoot.
I'd like you to investigate them.
They might refer to something other than places, too.
Please keep that in mind.
And we mustn't forget Laurier, the bay laurel.
I suspect that's connected to a place name as well.
Remember what the psalm says, too.
That's what the psalm says.
But we don't know where the clues might be hidden,
so I'll come along. The more minds we have working on it, the better.
Now, get ready.
As soon as you're ready, we'll leave for @6rWatering Labyrinth@0r.
You received the @3rBook of Demons@0r.
Back at the tavern, you hand @7rAnselm@0r the @3rNameless Book@0r.
Ah, welcome back. You brought it, then.
Is it your imagination, or does @7rAnselm@0r
look somehow frightened?
It certainly lives up to its reputation as a book stolen from a demon.
I can almost feel its sinister aura.
Here's your reward. Please take it.
From @7rAnselm@0r, you received the @3rBook of Demons@0r as a reward.
Whether using this will bring good fortune or ill...
You feel you have just heard something too troubling to ignore,
but when you look at @7rAnselm@0r, he merely watches you
with his usual inscrutable expression.
At any rate, you have my thanks.
I'll begin studying this book now.
I want to do whatever I can to help @7rBeatrix@0r.
With that, @7rAnselm@0r leaves.
But can you really trust him?
Watching him walk away,
you cannot shake an unsettling chill.
Oh, have you already collected it?
Oh dear, not yet?
I'm counting on you. It may prove quite important.
Ah, have you decided to accept?
It would help me if you could get started soon.
Good. Thank you.
Beyond knowing he's somewhere in @6rDiemen Labyrinth@0r,
I really don't know anything.
In that sense, it may be a difficult job.
There's no great hurry.
But don't take that as an excuse to dawdle.
The man bears the name @7rCock Robin@0r, passed down through generations.
Well, I'm counting on you.
Oh, yes. As for the thief's appearance,
I hear he has a birthmark resembling a little bird on his face.
It's hereditary, apparently, so the current thief should have it too.
You have accepted a job to find the thief called @7rCock Robin@0r
and collect an object passed down from his ancestors.
Oh, you won't accept?
Well, it can't be helped...
It's not a particularly urgent job,
so please take care of it when you have time.
I have another job I'd like kept secret. Would you be interested?
Secret from @7rBeatrix@0r and @7rCarmine@0r as well, of course.
It's a search for a person. I need you to find a certain thief.
He's probably hiding somewhere in @6rDiemen Labyrinth@0r.
That thief's ancestor, back when @7rChu Lu Gah@0r was alive,
often took on work for him.
I'd like you to collect an item the thief possesses,
something passed down from his ancestors.
That's all there is to it. Simple, isn't it?
It is simpler than solving some peculiar riddle,
but why must it be kept secret even from @7rBeatrix@0r?
You cannot understand.
The item has a rather troubling history. It was stolen from a demon.

context: Beatrix assigns the Last Psalm investigation; Anselm privately requests the Nameless Book via Cock Robin.
decisions: Control tokens remain on their source rows and in their original sequence. Genuine sentence continuations retain row boundaries; other omitted subjects are restored from scene context. Unknown historical warrior gender stays neutral. Item names follow the shared glossary; established imported prose and provenance remain intact.
